why: Deconstructs lifetime value into a time-constrained profit metric (LTGP) and provides the specific margin math required to back-propagate an acquisition CAC target.
topics: [profit and contribution formulas, incrementality and holdouts, return rate]

Topics. profit and contribution formulas / delineating between LTV (revenue) and LTGP (gross profit). Calculating Day 0 LTGP by subtracting COGS, cost of delivery (shipping, pick/pack, 3PL handling), transaction fees, and refund rate from new customer AOV. Back-propagating CAC targets by dividing desired LTGP constraints (e.g., 30-day or 90-day) by an efficiency ratio (e.g., targeting the 2 to 3 band). return rate / isolating refunds to the LTGP side of the equation rather than CAC, since refunds are a product-quality constraint, not a paid-media efficiency constraint. incrementality and holdouts / establishing CAC floors using CPC minimums and maximum theoretical conversion rates (CAC = CPC / Conversion Rate) to model aggressive vs. conservative scale ceilings.

Look for. The strict definition of LTGP (Lifetime Gross Profit): Revenue - COGS - Cost of Delivery (shipping/3PL) - Transaction Fees - Refunds. The rule requiring a time constraint on LTGP (e.g., 30, 90, or 180 days) instead of abstract "lifetime" revenue. The CPG-specific "CAC Payback Period" metric where brands take an initial loss on Day 0 and track the breakeven timeline via subscription/replenishment profit. The exact formula for a CAC target: target LTGP divided by the desired efficiency ratio (with 2 to 3 being the optimal scaling band). The mathematical floor for CAC: (lowest acceptable CPC) / (highest realistic conversion rate). The rule excluding refund rates from CAC calculations to prevent false signals in paid media performance tracking.
